summary.title: Bench Press Strength Builder — 12-Week Upper/Lower
summary.jordanWelcome: I'm Jordan, your coach for the next 12 weeks. You came in with a 275lb bench press target — I've built the entire program around getting you there. Week 1 is your calibration week — the weights are set conservatively so you can focus on form and give me honest effort ratings after each set. I'll use your RPE data from this week to tune what comes next specifically to you — the more honest you are, the better your plan gets.

sessions.title: Upper Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline heavy upper — 5×5 bench at 170lbs, log honestly.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary strength movement — 75% of your 225lb 1RM sets the baseline for the 12-week progression toward 275lbs.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Mid-back thickness through the horizontal pull pattern — builds the lat engagement and upper back tightness that supports your bench press setup.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest development through the incline press pattern — builds the clavicular pec head that contributes to the bottom portion of your bench.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull that develops lat width and shoulder girdle stability — a strong lat base improves your ability to keep your back tight and retracted on the bench.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Tricep strength through the full press range — direct carryover to bench lockout, which is a common sticking point when chasing a 1RM PR.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator work — balances horizontal pressing volume and keeps the shoulder joint healthy across a 12-week bench-focused program.

sessions.title: Lower Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Calibration lower — 5×5 squat, log your effort honestly today.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bilateral leg strength movement — develops quads, glutes, and full lower body force output. Baseline week establishes your starting squat load for the program.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — targets the biceps femoris in a way the hip hinge alone cannot, completing hamstring development for balanced leg sessions.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Quad isolation finisher — targets the rectus femoris and VMO directly, providing stimulus the squat pattern cannot fully replicate at this rep range.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core stability — builds the bracing strength needed to maintain a rigid torso under load in squats and all bilateral lower body movements.

sessions.title: Upper Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume upper — 5×8 bench at 145lbs, feel every rep.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Volume day exposure to the bench at 85% of your heavy day load — higher rep sets build work capacity and technique consistency that feeds directly into your 1RM progress.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull that develops mid-back thickness and scapular retraction strength — keeps pulling volume balanced against the increased pressing frequency of this bench-focused program.

exercises.name: Cable Chest Fly
exercises.coachingNote: Chest isolation through horizontal adduction — targets pec stretch and contraction in a way the press pattern cannot, adding volume for chest hypertrophy without extra pressing load on the shoulders.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull with a supinated grip emphasising lower lat and bicep engagement — complements the wide-grip pulldown from Monday with a different angle and motor pattern.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Tricep isolation focusing on the lateral head through the rope attachment — builds the arm extension strength that contributes to bench lockout at higher intensities.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Bicep development through elbow flexion — maintains arm balance alongside tricep and pressing work, and supports the supinated grip strength used in rows and pulldowns.

sessions.title: Lower Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume lower — hamstrings and glutes, 3 quality sets each.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge that builds hamstring and glute strength through their full range of motion — primary movement for this posterior-chain focused volume day.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Primary glute strength exercise through end-range hip extension — the hip thrust places peak load at full extension, a position the RDL and squat pattern cannot replicate.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation at longer muscle length — the seated position increases the stretch on the biceps femoris compared to the lying variation, adding quality hamstring volume to close out the week.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Glute medius isolation through hip abduction — the outer glute is undertrained by hinge and thrust patterns alone; this closes the gap and supports hip stability across all lower body work.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core exercise that demands full-length trunk stability — builds the deep abdominal and hip flexor control needed to maintain neutral spine under load.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Direct plantar flexion work for the gastrocnemius — builds lower leg mass and ankle stability that is underdeveloped by compound lower body movements alone.

sessions.title: Push Heavy

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise

exercises.name: Cable Fly (High to Low)
exercises.coachingNote: High-to-low cable angle emphasises the lower chest fibres and keeps tension through the full range of motion — something a barbell cannot replicate at the stretched position.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.coachingNote: The rope attachment allows the hands to flare at the bottom, increasing the peak contraction on the lateral tricep head. Used here as a high-rep finisher to accumulate tricep volume after the heavier compound work.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the rear delt and external rotators — muscles chronically underdeveloped in push-dominant programmes. Balances horizontal pressing volume and maintains shoulder joint health across a high-frequency week.

sessions.title: Pull Heavy

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull that develops lat width through a long range of motion — the wide grip keeps the elbows flared and places maximum tension on the outer lats at the stretched position.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Mid-back thickness builder — the seated cable position maintains constant tension through the full range and allows a deliberate eccentric that free weights cannot match. Targets the rhomboids and mid-traps alongside the lats.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Pulldown
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the lats by removing elbow flexion — the biceps cannot assist, so all force production comes from the lat. Excellent for building the mind-muscle connection and accumulating direct lat volume.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: The incline position places the long head of the bicep in a stretched position at the start of every rep — this lengthened loading is one of the most effective stimuli for bicep peak development.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip trains the brachialis and brachioradialis alongside the long head of the bicep — adds arm thickness and overall elbow flexor mass that a standard supinated curl alone will not develop.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrug
exercises.coachingNote: Direct upper trap isolation — the dumbbells allow a natural scapular arc that a barbell restricts. Upper trap mass contributes to the overall back thickness that supports a developed physique from every angle.

sessions.title: Legs Quad

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bilateral quad compound — the back squat develops quad, glute, and posterior chain strength simultaneously. As your top priority muscle group, this is the most important exercise of the week and anchors all lower body volume.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.coachingNote: The machine angle places the torso upright and shifts load directly onto the quads with less spinal demand than the barbell squat — ideal as a second quad compound to drive additional volume without systemic fatigue.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: The hip thrust loads the glutes at full hip extension — the point of maximum glute activation — which squats and hinges cannot replicate. Added here as extra glute volume given glutes are a stated priority muscle.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Direct quad isolation that trains the rectus femoris through its full shortening range — something compound squatting cannot achieve. Essential as a finisher to maximise quad volume after the heavy bilateral work.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation via knee flexion — trains the biceps femoris and semimembranosus independently of the glutes. Completes the hamstring stimulus started by the RDL with isolation volume for the priority muscle group.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core exercise that trains the rectus abdominis and deep stabilisers under a high eccentric load. Heavy squatting demands a strong bracing pattern — this movement develops that capacity directly.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-rotation core exercise that challenges the obliques and deep stabilisers to resist lateral force — a different stimulus to anti-extension work. Builds the rotational stability needed to stay tight under a loaded bar.

sessions.title: Push Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume push — 5 sets per exercise, feel the pump through chest.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest compound that shifts pressing load to the clavicular pec fibres and anterior delt. Using the barbell on volume day after dumbbell incline on heavy day provides a different loading stimulus to the same muscle fibres.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Mid-chest compound using dumbbells on volume day — the greater range of motion compared to a barbell provides a deeper pec stretch and higher time under tension per rep, supporting hypertrophy at moderate loads.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.coachingNote: Machine pressing on volume day removes stability demands and allows higher rep ranges with better fatigue management — the delt can be trained closer to failure without the stability risk of a barbell overhead press later in the week.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Cable version of the lateral raise maintains constant tension throughout the movement — unlike dumbbells which have a strength curve that drops off at the bottom. Used on volume day to accumulate medial delt stimulus after dumbbell laterals on Monday.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Machine fly that isolates the mid chest through pure horizontal adduction without any tricep involvement — allows the pec to be taken to full failure safely, making it a high-value chest isolation finisher.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Overhead position places the long head of the tricep in a fully stretched position at the start of each rep — the long head makes up the majority of tricep mass and is best developed with overhead loading.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (V-Bar)
exercises.coachingNote: V-bar attachment emphasises the lateral tricep head with a neutral grip — used here after the overhead extension to cover both the long and lateral heads across the session and accumulate high tricep volume on volume day.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt isolation on the pec deck machine — trains horizontal shoulder abduction and external rotation, balancing the heavy pressing volume accumulated over two push sessions this week.

exercises.coachingNote: Mid-back thickness compound — the T-bar neutral grip and chest support option keeps fatigue out of the lower back on volume day while producing high mechanical tension through the rhomboids, traps, and lats.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Reverse grip shifts the elbow path inward and increases bicep contribution while placing a strong stretch on the lower lats — a different pull stimulus to the wide-grip version used Monday, developing fuller lat development.

exercises.name: Cable Row (Single Arm)
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral cable rowing removes the dominant side from compensating and forces each side to produce equal force — identifies and corrects strength imbalances while adding mid-back volume with a full rotational range.

exercises.name: Meadows Row
exercises.coachingNote: Landmine-anchored unilateral row that loads the lat through a long arc with a strong stretch at extension — the angled pull path hits the outer lat differently from any standard horizontal row and adds overall back width.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Bilateral barbell curl allows maximum loading for the bicep short head and overall elbow flexor mass — the fixed bar path enables overloading beyond what single-arm variations permit, driving overall bicep thickness.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: The preacher pad locks the upper arm and removes shoulder flexion cheating — the bicep must complete the full contraction without momentum, making this the most targeted short-head and overall curl mass builder.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.coachingNote: Cable fly variation for the rear delt and infraspinatus — cable tension keeps resistance constant through the full arc, unlike dumbbells. Placed on pull day to accumulate rear delt volume alongside horizontal pulling work.

sessions.title: Legs Posterior
sessions.sessionFocus: Posterior chain focus — calibrate RDL and hip thrust for 5 sets.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Primary hip hinge for the posterior chain session — the stiff-leg variation keeps a minimal knee bend throughout, maximising the stretch and load through the hamstrings at the bottom. Your heaviest hamstring movement of the week.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Machine hip thrust keeps the load path consistent and removes stability demands — allows heavier loading and better glute isolation than the floor barbell version. As a priority muscle, glutes receive dedicated heavy compound work this session.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Priority quad exercise added to this posterior session — unilateral loading exposes and corrects strength asymmetries while the rear-foot elevation increases quad stretch depth. Ensures quads receive volume across all lower body sessions.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position places the hamstring under stretch at the hip, increasing long-head loading — a different stimulus to lying leg curl. Used here as an isolation finisher to complete hamstring volume after the heavy hinge compound.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge with constant cable tension throughout — specifically loads the glute-hamstring tie-in at the bottom of the movement. Adds glute isolation volume without additional spinal loading late in a posterior chain session.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the gluteus medius and minimus through hip abduction — the outer glute fibres that hip thrusts and hinges do not directly target. Glute med development adds both width and functional stability to the hip complex.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: The seated position bends the knee and takes the gastrocnemius off tension, shifting the load entirely to the soleus — the deeper calf muscle responsible for lower leg thickness. Pairs with standing raises in later weeks.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core exercise that trains the lower rectus abdominis and hip flexors through a long range of motion — balances the anti-extension core work from Wednesday with a different stimulus pattern to complete weekly core volume.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation via knee flexion — trains the biceps femoris and semimembranosus independently of the glutes. Completes the hamstring stimulus started by the RDL with isolation volume for the priority muscle group.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core exercise that trains the rectus abdominis and deep stabilisers under a high eccentric load. Heavy squatting demands a strong bracing pattern — this movement develops that capacity directly.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-rotation core exercise that challenges the obliques and deep stabilisers to resist lateral force — a different stimulus to anti-extension work. Builds the rotational stability needed to stay tight under a loaded bar.

days.title: Push Volume
days.sessionFocus: Volume push — 5 sets per exercise, feel the pump through chest.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest compound that shifts pressing load to the clavicular pec fibres and anterior delt. Using the barbell on volume day after dumbbell incline on heavy day provides a different loading stimulus to the same muscle fibres.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Mid-chest compound using dumbbells on volume day — the greater range of motion compared to a barbell provides a deeper pec stretch and higher time under tension per rep, supporting hypertrophy at moderate loads.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.coachingNote: Machine pressing on volume day removes stability demands and allows higher rep ranges with better fatigue management — the delt can be trained closer to failure without the stability risk of a barbell overhead press later in the week.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Cable version of the lateral raise maintains constant tension throughout the movement — unlike dumbbells which have a strength curve that drops off at the bottom. Used on volume day to accumulate medial delt stimulus after dumbbell laterals on Monday.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Machine fly that isolates the mid chest through pure horizontal adduction without any tricep involvement — allows the pec to be taken to full failure safely, making it a high-value chest isolation finisher.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension (Rope)

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (V-Bar)
exercises.coachingNote: V-bar attachment emphasises the lateral tricep head with a neutral grip — used here after the overhead extension to cover both the long and lateral heads across the session and accumulate high tricep volume on volume day.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt isolation on the pec deck machine — trains horizontal shoulder abduction and external rotation, balancing the heavy pressing volume accumulated over two push sessions this week.

days.title: Pull Volume
days.sessionFocus: Volume pull — 5 sets, target upper back thickness and bicep pump.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Reverse grip shifts the elbow path inward and increases bicep contribution while placing a strong stretch on the lower lats — a different pull stimulus to the wide-grip version used Monday, developing fuller lat development.

exercises.name: Cable Row (Single Arm)
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral cable rowing removes the dominant side from compensating and forces each side to produce equal force — identifies and corrects strength imbalances while adding mid-back volume with a full rotational range.

exercises.name: Meadows Row
exercises.coachingNote: Landmine-anchored unilateral row that loads the lat through a long arc with a strong stretch at extension — the angled pull path hits the outer lat differently from any standard horizontal row and adds overall back width.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Bilateral barbell curl allows maximum loading for the bicep short head and overall elbow flexor mass — the fixed bar path enables overloading beyond what single-arm variations permit, driving overall bicep thickness.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: The preacher pad locks the upper arm and removes shoulder flexion cheating — the bicep must complete the full contraction without momentum, making this the most targeted short-head and overall curl mass builder.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.coachingNote: Cable fly variation for the rear delt and infraspinatus — cable tension keeps resistance constant through the full arc, unlike dumbbells. Placed on pull day to accumulate rear delt volume alongside horizontal pulling work.

days.title: Legs Posterior
days.sessionFocus: Posterior chain focus — calibrate RDL and hip thrust for 5 sets.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Primary hip hinge for the posterior chain session — the stiff-leg variation keeps a minimal knee bend throughout, maximising the stretch and load through the hamstrings at the bottom. Your heaviest hamstring movement of the week.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Machine hip thrust keeps the load path consistent and removes stability demands — allows heavier loading and better glute isolation than the floor barbell version. As a priority muscle, glutes receive dedicated heavy compound work this session.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Priority quad exercise added to this posterior session — unilateral loading exposes and corrects strength asymmetries while the rear-foot elevation increases quad stretch depth. Ensures quads receive volume across all lower body sessions.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position places the hamstring under stretch at the hip, increasing long-head loading — a different stimulus to lying leg curl. Used here as an isolation finisher to complete hamstring volume after the heavy hinge compound.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge with constant cable tension throughout — specifically loads the glute-hamstring tie-in at the bottom of the movement. Adds glute isolation volume without additional spinal loading late in a posterior chain session.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the gluteus medius and minimus through hip abduction — the outer glute fibres that hip thrusts and hinges do not directly target. Glute med development adds both width and functional stability to the hip complex.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: The seated position bends the knee and takes the gastrocnemius off tension, shifting the load entirely to the soleus — the deeper calf muscle responsible for lower leg thickness. Pairs with standing raises in later weeks.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core exercise that trains the lower rectus abdominis and hip flexors through a long range of motion — balances the anti-extension core work from Wednesday with a different stimulus pattern to complete weekly core volume.

Week 1 is your calibration week — pick loads that match your effort targets and record them after each set, because that data is how I tune what comes next. I'll use your RPE data from this week to tune what comes next specifically to you — the more honest you are, the better your plan gets.

sessions.title: Push Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline push — find your working weights across 4 sets.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary horizontal push for this session — trains the pec major, anterior delt, and triceps together and serves as the anchor compound for upper body pressing strength.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: The incline angle shifts stress toward the clavicular head of the pec — a region the flat bench underdevelops and a key marker of balanced chest hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the medial deltoid through its full range of motion — compound pressing does not adequately develop this head, and cable tension keeps load consistent at the top where it matters most.

exercises.name: Cable Fly (High to Low)
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the lower and mid pec through full adduction range — the cable maintains tension at peak contraction where dumbbells lose it, making this a superior isolation finisher.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the triceps through the full pressing range under heavy load — the narrow grip shifts emphasis away from the pec and onto all three tricep heads with direct carryover to bench lockout.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.coachingNote: The rope attachment allows the handles to flare outward at the bottom, maximising lateral head contraction and elbow extension range — an isolation finisher that accumulates volume the compound movements cannot match.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator work that directly counterbalances the heavy horizontal pressing volume in this session — keeps the shoulder joint healthy across a high-volume training block.

sessions.title: Pull Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline pull — log your heaviest comfortable set on rows.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)
exercises.coachingNote: Wide overhand grip targets the upper back, rhomboids, and rear delts with significant lat engagement — your primary heavy horizontal pull and the anchor compound for back thickness.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Wide grip pulldown emphasises lat width through shoulder adduction — pairs with the horizontal row to cover both movement planes and ensures full back development within the session.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: A second horizontal pull that adds mid-back and lat volume with constant cable tension throughout the full range — reduces spinal loading compared to the barbell row while accumulating additional back thickness work.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Pulldown
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the lat through shoulder extension with the elbow locked — removes bicep involvement entirely and creates direct lat tension from a long lengthened position, which is a strong hypertrophy stimulus.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Bilateral barbell curl loads the short head of the bicep and allows heavier absolute loading than unilateral work — your primary bicep mass builder on this heavy pull day.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip shifts emphasis to the brachialis and long head of the bicep — develops elbow flexor thickness and arm width that the standard curl does not fully address.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrug
exercises.coachingNote: Direct upper trap work through scapular elevation — the upper traps contribute to the overall back thickness and shoulder appearance that compound rows alone leave underdeveloped.

sessions.title: Legs Quad
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline quads — calibrate squat load across 4 working sets.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: The primary bilateral squat pattern trains quads, glutes, and core under heavy axial load — your main lower body strength compound and the session anchor for quad-dominant development.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Machine-based squat pattern that places the torso upright, maximising knee travel and quad activation — allows additional quad volume without the spinal loading of a second free-weight squat.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral quad and glute work that addresses side-to-side imbalances a bilateral squat cannot expose — high single-leg demand with significant stretch-mediated hypertrophy stimulus through the working limb.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Quad isolation through knee extension — removes glute and hamstring contribution entirely, delivering direct rectus femoris and vastus stress that compound patterns cannot replicate at this intensity level.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — complements the RDL's hip-extension focus and ensures the biceps femoris is loaded through both joints, which is the complete stimulus for hamstring hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Hip flexion and lower abdominal flexion under load — builds the anterior core strength needed to maintain bracing during heavy compound lower body work throughout the week.

sessions.title: Upper Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume upper — 4 sets each, chase quality reps at RPE 8.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest compound that opens the volume upper day — the incline barbell allows heavier loading than the incline dumbbell variation and drives clavicular pec development from a second weekly angle.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral horizontal pull that allows greater range of motion and lat stretch than the bilateral barbell row — accumulates mid-back and lat volume on the second back session of the week.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Machine fly that trains the pec through full horizontal adduction with constant tension — provides high-quality stretch stimulus at the start of the range that pressing movements cannot replicate.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Reverse grip shifts the wrist into supination and increases bicep engagement while maintaining vertical pull mechanics — targets the lower lat and inner back from a different angle than the wide grip used on Pull Heavy day.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Second medial delt session of the week — shoulder width requires significant direct lateral head volume and two dedicated sessions per week is appropriate for an advanced athlete targeting balanced upper body development.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl
exercises.coachingNote: EZ bar position reduces wrist strain during bilateral curling and places the bicep in a slightly different supination angle than the straight barbell — second bicep session of the week for full development stimulus.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Overhead position places the long head of the tricep in a fully lengthened position — the long head is the largest of the three and responds strongly to the stretch stimulus this movement provides.

sessions.title: Lower Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Posterior chain volume — hinge and glute focus across 4 sets.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Hip extension with peak glute contraction at full lockout — the horizontally loaded pattern isolates the glute max more effectively than any squat or hinge variation and serves as the primary glute compound for this session.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge with minimal knee bend that maximises hamstring length under load — a second weekly posterior chain hinge session drives hamstring hypertrophy through the full range of hip flexion to extension.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position keeps the hip flexed during the curl, placing the biceps femoris in a more lengthened starting position than the lying variation — research supports this positioning for superior hamstring hypertrophy stimulus.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Hip abduction isolates the gluteus medius — a muscle the hip thrust and hinge patterns leave largely untrained and one that contributes to glute shape and hip stability during all lower body movements.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Gastrocnemius-dominant calf movement performed with a straight knee — the gastrocnemius crosses the knee joint and is only fully recruited in the extended position, making this the primary calf mass builder.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Knee-flexed position removes the gastrocnemius and isolates the soleus — the soleus responds to higher rep ranges and adds calf thickness that the standing variation cannot target.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-rotation core exercise that trains the obliques and deep stabilisers to resist lateral force — develops the rotational bracing strength that underpins safe mechanics across every compound movement in this plan.

summary.title: Full Body Foundations — 8-Week Dumbbell Plan
summary.jordanWelcome: I'm Jordan, your coach for the next 8 weeks. You want to build a consistent fitness base — I've kept the program structured but manageable so you can build the habit first, and Week 1 you set your own starting weights in the app, aiming for something that feels like RPE 6 on each exercise. Week 1 is your calibration week — pick loads that match your effort targets and record them after each set; that data is how I tune what comes next. I'll use your RPE data from this week to tune what comes next specifically to you — the more honest you are, the better your plan gets.

sessions.title: Full Body A
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline full body — 2 sets each, log effort honestly.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary horizontal push — trains the pecs, front delt, and triceps together as the anchor compound for this session.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the lats and mid-back through a horizontal pull — pairs directly with the pressing work to keep shoulder loading balanced.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.coachingNote: A beginner-friendly squat pattern that develops quad and glute strength while the goblet position teaches you to stay upright through the movement.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.coachingNote: An anti-extension core exercise that trains the deep abdominals to resist lumbar extension — builds the trunk stability your compound lifts rely on.

sessions.title: Full Body B
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline full body B — shoulder and hinge focus, 2 sets each.

exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.coachingNote: A vertical push that develops all three heads of the deltoid — the rotation through the press recruits the medial and rear delt more than a standard press.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull that develops mid-back thickness and lat strength — balances the pressing volume from Tuesday and keeps shoulder mechanics healthy.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary hip hinge — trains the hamstrings and glutes through their full range and teaches the foundational hinge pattern that underpins all posterior chain work.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core work that trains the entire anterior trunk to maintain a rigid, neutral spine position — directly supports your hinge and pressing mechanics.

sessions.title: Full Body A
sessions.sessionFocus: Second Full Body A — match Tuesday's effort, 2 sets each.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: An incline angle shifts emphasis toward the upper chest and front delt — varying the press angle from Tuesday ensures balanced chest development across the week.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull that trains the lats and mid-back through a unilateral pattern — using the same movement as Tuesday lets you build consistency with the technique across Week 1.

exercises.name: Walking Lunge
exercises.coachingNote: A single-leg squat-pattern movement that builds quad and glute strength while training balance and hip stability — complements Tuesday's goblet squat with a unilateral challenge.

exercises.name: Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: A flexion-based core exercise that targets the lower abdominals — complements the anti-extension work from earlier in the week with a different core demand.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip targets the brachialis and brachioradialis alongside the bicep — adds arm thickness that supinated curls alone won't fully develop.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (Rope)

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — the lying position places the hip in extension which increases the stretch on the biceps femoris relative to seated variations.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the gastrocnemius through plantar flexion with a straight knee — direct calf volume that compound lower body movements do not provide in meaningful amounts.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)
exercises.coachingNote: Overhand wide-grip row shifts the stimulus toward the upper back and rear delt while still loading the lats through horizontal pull — pairs with the vertical pull above to develop the back through both movement planes.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Pulldown
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the lat through shoulder extension with the elbow locked — removes bicep involvement entirely so the lat does all the work, making it an efficient lat-specific finisher.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: A second horizontal pull to add mid-back and lat thickness volume — cable constant tension throughout the range of motion means the muscle stays loaded at full stretch, maximising hypertrophic stimulus.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: The incline position places the long head of the bicep in a stretched position at the bottom of every rep — this lengthened-position loading is the most effective way to target the long head for peak development.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip targets the long head of the bicep and the brachialis underneath it — adding brachialis size pushes the bicep up visually, contributing to arm thickness and peak height.

exercises.name: Bayesian Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Cable behind the body extends the shoulder slightly, stretching the long head under load at the start of every rep — this is a long-head priority exercise that complements the incline curl earlier in the session.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator work to balance the horizontal pressing volume from Monday — keeps shoulder health in check across a high-frequency upper body program.

days.title: Legs Full (Quad Focus)
days.sessionFocus: Quad-dominant baseline — 5 heavy sets on back squat first.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: The primary bilateral squat pattern — develops quad, glute, and posterior chain strength through a full range of motion and is the anchor compound for the quad-focused session.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Fixed-path machine allows deeper knee flexion with a more upright torso than the barbell squat — this increases quad recruitment and allows more volume without the spinal loading of a second barbell movement.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation that trains the knee flexion function of the muscle — the RDL trains hip extension but does not fully train knee flexion, so this exercise fills that gap.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Glute-dominant hip extension at a horizontal load angle — produces higher glute EMG than squatting or hinging patterns and adds direct glute volume to round out the lower body session.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Quad isolation at the knee — the only exercise in this session that trains knee extension without hip involvement, allowing the quad to be targeted directly as a finishing movement.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core exercise that trains the lower abdominals and hip flexors through a full range of motion — heavier and more demanding than floor-based alternatives, appropriate for an advanced lifter.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core movement — trains the ability to resist lumbar extension under load, which directly supports bracing quality in squats and hinge movements.

days.title: Upper Volume
days.sessionFocus: Volume upper — chest, back, and arms across 8 exercises.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest emphasis on a barbell for higher loading potential than dumbbells — accumulates chest volume at a moderate rep range after the heavy bench work earlier in the week.

exercises.name: Cable Fly (Mid Cable)
exercises.coachingNote: Mid-cable fly trains the pec through its full adduction range with constant tension — effective as a volume accumulation tool for overall chest development on the second chest session of the week.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.coachingNote: Bodyweight vertical pull that loads the lats and upper back through full shoulder depression — used here as the anchor back compound on the volume upper day to continue lat priority development.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral horizontal pull that allows a greater range of motion and stretch than barbell rowing — trains the lat, mid-back, and rear delt with independent arm loading to address side-to-side imbalances.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Reverse grip shifts the elbow path closer to the torso and increases lat engagement at the bottom of the pull — a different angle than the wide-grip work on Tuesday to stimulate new motor patterns in the lat.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Wide grip on the EZ bar reduces wrist supination slightly but keeps emphasis on the long head — a barbell-style loading pattern that allows heavier loads than dumbbell work for additional long-head volume.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Preacher pad fixes the upper arm in front of the body, eliminating shoulder flexion cheating and placing the short head under maximum tension — balances the long-head bias from the other bicep work this week.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (V-Bar)
exercises.coachingNote: V-bar pushdown trains the lateral and medial tricep heads through elbow extension at a fixed angle — adds isolation volume for the tricep on the second upper session without duplicating the rope or overhead work from Monday.

days.title: Lower Volume
days.sessionFocus: Posterior chain volume — hamstrings and glutes, 5 sets each.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Primary hip hinge for the posterior chain session — keeps the knee more extended than a Romanian deadlift, placing maximum stretch and tension on the hamstrings through their full length.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Machine hip thrust allows heavier loading with better stability than barbell variations — trains the glute at the shortened position where hip extension force output peaks, complementing the hinge work above.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position keeps the hip slightly flexed, which increases the stretch on the hamstring at the start of the movement — a complementary isolation angle to the lying curl used on Wednesday.

exercises.name: Single Leg RDL
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral hinge that challenges hamstring and glute strength independently on each leg — exposes and corrects side-to-side imbalances that bilateral hinge work can mask.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the glute medius through hip abduction — this portion of the glute is undertrained by hinging and hip thrust patterns and contributes to hip stability and glute width.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the gastrocnemius through plantar flexion with the knee extended — the primary calf mass builder and the standard first calf movement for an advanced lower body session.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Knee bent position shifts the load to the soleus, which lies beneath the gastrocnemius — training both muscles is required to develop full lower leg size and cannot be achieved with standing calf raises alone.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-rotation core exercise that trains the obliques and deep stabilisers to resist rotational force — a different core stimulus than the flexion and anti-extension work programmed on Wednesday.
